tour.title: Start At The Entry Points
tour.description: Begin with the backend and the two client bootstraps to see how Trenfy starts up across server, web, and mobile surfaces.
tour.languageLesson: Entry files usually reveal composition roots and dependency direction.

tour.title: Trace The Backend API
tour.description: Read the FastAPI app, trend routes, and contracts together to understand the public backend surface consumed by clients.
tour.languageLesson: Typed API contracts make backend changes easier to reason about.

tour.title: Follow Trend Processing
tour.description: These workflow and shared-agent modules show how source data is scheduled, normalized, and moved through the backend.
tour.languageLesson: Keep orchestration separate from model definitions so state shape stays clear.

tour.title: Inspect External Integrations
tour.description: The tool layer contains the adapters that talk to NocoDB, OpenAI, X, YouTube, translation, and HTML extraction helpers.
tour.languageLesson: Adapter modules reduce the amount of third-party detail that leaks into core workflows.

tour.title: Walk The Web Admin
tour.description: These React files cover app bootstrap, major admin pages, shared layout, and the API client boundary in the web experience.
tour.languageLesson: Web UI is easier to follow when pages, shared layout, and API wrappers are read together.

tour.title: Walk The Mobile App
tour.description: The mobile files show how the white-label experience is composed from screens, reusable cards, seeded content, and theme tokens.
tour.languageLesson: Token-driven mobile apps centralize brand styling and keep screens lightweight.

tour.title: Finish With Validation And Ops
tour.description: Tests and deployment files close the loop by showing how the system is verified and configured outside runtime code.
tour.languageLesson: Operational files and tests are part of the architecture, not just scaffolding.
